live_media.host: macOS arm64, Home Assistant Core and headless Chrome
live_media.source: FFmpeg 9.0.2 testsrc2 with red or blue marker, Nxrs RTSP publisher and loopback MediaMTX. No physical camera or microphone.
live_media.negative_control: Before local End removed its SDK entry, both browser peers observed source loss but a direct CurrentSessions read still returned two rows after five seconds.
limitations: The two viewers used the same commissioned fabric and isolated MediaMTX internal authorization. Nxrs strict media admission, per-fabric revocation and simultaneous Nxrs Home playback require qualification.
The bounded share queue admits at most eight access units of at most 1 MiB each. Maximum memory used by the RTSP library during packet assembly remains unmeasured.
Browser presentation with generated video does not qualify physical camera, microphone, iPhone, Linux, remote access or soak performance.

strict_media_access.source: Generated FFmpeg video through the Nxrs RTSP publisher and private MediaMTX with HTTP authorization by real strict Nxrs gateway control. Pinned macOS SDK, commissioned Home Assistant and headless Chrome; independent RTSP readers used PyAV 16.1.0.
qualification_notes: Retirement time runs from fault injection to a direct Matter CurrentSessions read showing zero entries. Browser presented FPS is diagnostic. All three experiments used the same isolated commissioning and account state in Home Assistant and fresh gateway enrollments per run.

The revocation experiment had three upstream readers: one shared Matter input and two independent RTSP decoders. Only the revoked source and its non-renewing decoder were retired before the gateway restart. The other decoder advanced at least 15 more frames and the publisher kept its session ID. Existing readers are reconciled as unowned after the gateway restarts.
open: Selective removal of one Matter fabric/controller while another uses the same source, runtime ownership barriers, physical input and concurrent Nxrs Home/iPhone playback, microphone, Linux/remote qualification and soak.

audio_publication.source: One FFmpeg generator produces a timed light pattern and matching 1 kHz tone on a shared clock. The Nxrs publisher sends H.264 and mono Opus in one session to MediaMTX under strict gateway authorization. PyAV decodes both tracks over RTSP/TCP.
audio_publication.scope: Opt-in timestamped publication on the host. Cue differences use decoded timestamps at 15 fps, with 20 ms audio. They do not measure microphone capture latency, rendered iPhone lip sync or long-run drift. The existing camera ingest, Matter reader and iPhone have no newly qualified audio path.

multi_admin.source: One isolated FFmpeg video generator, Nxrs publisher, MediaMTX, gateway under strict authorization, RTSP bridge and independent matter-server controllers with distinct CA stores. Both receivers used aiortc on the same Mac.
qualification_notes: Allow two seconds for packets in flight after successful RemoveFabric. Keep both receiver peers open for the following four measured seconds. The removed receiver sends no EndSession. The surviving viewer and the original publisher and reader stay connected.

After restart the authorized administrator read the complete device fabric table. It contained only the surviving fabric, then the surviving and the new fabric after commissioning. The retired controller read outcome is reported separately. A transport timeout establishes only that no authenticated response was observed during the measured interval.

For index wrap, the surviving administrator removed each replacement fabric using OperationalCredentials.RemoveFabric. A fresh controller store and CA were used per enrolment. The 253rd replacement received the retired index. The original controller returned an error for an operational read; the surviving administrator directly verified the replacement's membership. An earlier stress attempt using one repeatedly recycled controller store stopped at AddNOC InvalidNOC with the device allocation cursor at 128; this distinct controller-reuse case is unqualified.
open: Individual node permissions within a fabric, interrupted multi-admin mutations, joined worker cleanup, physical audio/video, iPhone, Linux, remote access and soak.

audio_allocation.scope: One independent Matter Server commissioned a macOS test node. The strict gateway authorized one RTSP source reader and generated video/Opus. This verifies camera-cluster commands and the table read from the device. The WebRTC path still sends video only. Neither audible Matter playback nor hardware microphone capture, mute, privacy or active audio-reference ownership is qualified.

matter_microphone_playback.scope: Generated H.264/Opus through one authorized source reader per trial. The browser light-to-tone offsets use requestVideoFrameCallback and a Web Audio analyser on the incoming track. They include browser scheduling and analysis delay. Hardware capture, acoustic playout, iPhone timing, long-run drift, microphone mute and privacy remain open.

matter_viewer_privacy.receiver: Commissioned Matter Server and independent aiortc peer using generated H.264 and pulsed mono Opus.
matter_viewer_privacy.scope: The Matter endpoint and receiving peer ran on macOS. The source produced a known generated tone. Physical microphone capture, effects on non-Matter recording and detection, iPhone playback and physical A/V timing remain open.

operator_commissioning.scope: A real independent Matter Server commissioned a generated-media node on the Mac with the SDK development attestation chain. The passcode stayed with the operator. Physical iPhone scanning, production attestation, interrupted fabric removal, Linux discovery and physical media remain open.

same_fabric_camera_access.host: macOS arm64, isolated generated H.264 publication, pinned Matter Server and a separately commissioned Matter.js requestor
same_fabric_camera_access.measurement: Both controllers decoded 20 frames concurrently and appeared under distinct node IDs on the same fabric. After the revoked controller received NoUserMedia, allow one second to drain in-flight media, then count received RTP and decoded frames at both receivers for four seconds. The restored endpoint grant admitted a new session after restoration.
same_fabric_camera_access.scope: WebRTC offer permission at camera endpoint 1, including an established viewer and an unanswered offer. Full process-loss recovery during administration, production admission, Linux and physical device/audio qualification remain open.

interrupted_access_changes.host: macOS arm64, LLDB 2103.0.34.103, generated video, independent operational nodes
interrupted_access_changes.scope: Each fresh process reused its original enrollment. The debugger interrupted the actual ACL update or fabric-key deletion in the published SDK fixture. Other per-fabric records, interrupted commissioning, machine power loss, Linux and physical media need separate qualification.

source_bound_offers.scope: A commissioned host fixture consumed one authenticated RTSP input and terminated two distinct pending negotiations on source replacement. Physical camera and microphone, iPhone playback and joined worker retirement under load remain open.

configured_camera.host: macOS arm64 with isolated Matter Server, generated H.264 and detection fixtures, MediaMTX and strict gateway control
configured_camera.scope: This fixture exercises one Matter camera and its occupancy endpoint. A second configured gateway camera was used to check source selection. Multi-camera endpoint allocation, discovery on selected Linux/macOS interfaces, physical playback and microphone remain release work.

joined_sessions.host: macOS arm64, two independent Matter controllers, generated H.264
joined_sessions.scope: Joined peer resource release for explicit EndSession, cancellation of pending offers and removal of one of two fabrics. The test checks each live peer’s actual nominated UDP port. Long offline signaling deadlines, full process shutdown under load, physical cameras and iPhone remain separate tests.

jpeg_snapshots.host: macOS arm64, pinned Matter Server, generated H.264
jpeg_snapshots.scope: JPEG allocation, scaling, capture, reuse, immediate rate-limit rejection, unavailable and private admission, and encoder reaping before an in-flight source-loss rejection. Concurrent Matter command responsiveness, production conformance, privacy changes made during encoding through an independent access path, and physical capture remain open.

graceful_shutdown.host: macOS arm64, two isolated Matter Server fabrics, generated H.264
graceful_shutdown.scope: Separate unanswered SDP and incomplete ICE, two failed outbound deliveries while their controller is suspended, retirement and continuing decoded video on another fabric. Joined SIGTERM with an established peer, a pending peer and a blocked JPEG encoder, followed by playback on the same publication and preserved enrollment. A separate Matter read completes during capture. Final-fabric cleanup, physical audio/video, production wide-area timing and soak remain open.

final_fabric_removal.host: macOS arm64, pinned Matter Server, generated H.264
final_fabric_removal.baseline: The shutdown fixture removed the last fabric but retained the changed label and camera installation records on disk.
final_fabric_removal.scope: Last-fabric removal, selective removal with one survivor, invitation closure, existing playback retirement, settings and subscription cleanup, and recovery across the durable rename while using configured endpoint identity. No live camera or production enrollments were used. Interrupted addition of a fabric, physical microphone and production root-node conformance remain open.

interrupted_commissioning.host: macOS arm64, pinned Matter Server, wired bridge fixture with generated H.264

baseline.scenario: First enrollment killed after storage sync and before the reply. The completed fabric remained but the original Matter Server had no commissioned node on restart.

interrupted_commissioning.scope: Process interruption before the atomic replacement and after directory sync on first and additional Ethernet-host enrollment. A fresh operator-opened window restores an abandoned first enrollment. A surviving administrator can withdraw an abandoned additional enrollment. No live camera, physical commissioning, wireless credentials, or direct NuttX behavior was exercised.

linux_runtime.negative_control: With the previous shutdown path, an active snapshot lost the TCP connection during restart. The independent controller logged ECONNREFUSED and scheduled a two-minute retry, exceeding the unchanged 35-second operational recovery check.
linux_runtime.scope: Discovery, configured ICE route, occupancy and independent media access, JPEG, retirement and persistence on the isolated Linux guest. The cross-platform shutdown regression verifies cancellation and controller stream release before exit, plus playback after restart with the same enrollment. Multi-interface scoping, physical traffic, iPhone presentation and soak require separate qualification.

lan_interface.linux: Debian 13.7 ARM64, Linux 6.12.117, native Avahi 0.8-16. Distinct peers on two veth IPv4 and IPv6 networks.
lan_interface.scope: Linux commissioning and operational IPv6 multicast on one selected link, IPv4 and IPv6 Matter TCP and UDP isolation including cross-link traffic to selected addresses, actual IPv6 Matter JPEG and IPv4 WebRTC, and same-enrollment restart with interface inference. macOS qualified the scoped build on its selected interface through discovery, decoded video, remapping and persistence. The Linux witness does not substitute for macOS two-link, physical iPhone, or wide-area tests.
